pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Bryanston Square CofE Primary School - Headteachers' Welcome
pageCache.text:
Headteachers' Welcome
Welcome to St Mary’s Bryanston Square CE Primary School, a beacon of excellence nestled in the heart of Marylebone, London. We pride ourselves on our outstanding behaviour, leadership, and personal development programs that shape our students into well-rounded individuals ready to excel in their future endeavors.
At St Mary's we are fortunate to have two Headteachers; Mr Duffy & Mrs Marius-Beeko.
Mr Duffy is our Executive Headteacher, who has responsibility for three schools (St Mary's Bryanston Square, Christ Church, Regents Park & St Mary's Magdalene & St Stephen's CE Primary School).
Mrs Marius-Beeko is the Head of School of St Mary's every day, leading our school.
We want all of our children to be able to make confident choices in the future, whether that is in the next phase of their education or in later life. We hope that the time in which they were with us, they will have gained the knowledge and skills to allow them to make choices in life, whichever route they take.
We have high expectations of all of our children at SMBS and use our school’s Christian values and the teachings of the Bible to help us live life in all its fullness. Our school vision of 'Excellence with Compassion'
drives all that we do.
St Mary’s Bryanston Square Primary School is not just any school; it is a village school in the heart of London, offering a unique blend of a close-knit community atmosphere with the rich cultural experiences of the city. Our prime location provides a safe, nurturing environment while being accessible to the myriad educational and recreational opportunities that London has to offer.
Mrs Marius-Beeko shares:
As Head of School, it is my privilege to lead a community where every child is known, valued and encouraged to thrive. At the heart of our work is our Christian vision of “Excellence with Compassion.” We believe that education should nurture both the mind and the spirit, and we are committed to ensuring that all children flourish within a caring and aspirational environment. Guided by our Christian ethos, we encourage our pupils to develop the curiosity, kindness and resilience that will set them up to life-long lovers of learning.
Our vision of Excellence with Compassion means that we seek the very best for every child. We challenge and support our pupils so that they make strong academic progress while also growing spiritually and morally. Through high expectations, inspiring teaching and a culture of care, we aim for each child to develop confidence, character and curiosity.
We are also proud to make the most of our exceptional Central London location. Our pupils benefit from enriching partnerships with world-renowned cultural institutions, including the Royal College of Music, the Royal Albert Hall and Sinfonia Smith Square. In addition, we regularly visit London Zoo as well as the many museums and galleries at the heart of our city. These experiences bring learning to life and ensure that our children engage with the very best of the arts, sciences and cultural heritage that London has to offer.
Our commitment to academic excellence is reflected in our national outcomes. In May 2023, Ofsted highlighted our achievements, stating, “Leaders have high expectations of all pupils, including those with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND). Pupils read enthusiastically. They learn a broad range of subjects and are taught how to make connections between subject content in different areas of the curriculum. Leaders’ work to develop the curriculum is rigorous, including in early years, where their actions have been particularly successful. They know what is working well, and they are tenacious in building on this and securing further improvements. This is a key reason why pupils learn so effectively in many subjects. Parents are extremely positive about the school. They comment that it feels like a family. Parents are extremely positive about the school. They comment that it feels like a family.”
At St Mary’s Bryanston Square, we are particularly proud of our expertise in phonics and music. As a lead school for both subjects, we have established innovative programs that ensure our students not only meet but exceed national standards. Our phonics program is designed to instill a strong foundation in reading from an early age, while our comprehensive music curriculum nurtures creativity and provides students with numerous performance opportunities, fostering both confidence and artistic expression.
Our Early Years department is another cornerstone of our school’s success. Recognized for its outstanding provision, our Early Years team creates a stimulating and supportive environment where young children can thrive. The dedication and expertise of our staff ensure that each child receives personalized attention, enabling them to develop a love for learning that lasts a lifetime.
Choosing St Mary’s Bryanston Square Primary School means choosing a school that values excellence in all areas. Our outstanding behaviour standards create a positive and respectful school culture, our strong leadership provides clear direction and support, and our focus on personal development ensures every child feels valued and empowered to achieve their best.
Join us at St Mary’s Bryanston Square Primary School, where every child’s potential is nurtured, and excellence is a tradition. Explore our website to learn more about our curriculum, achievements, and the vibrant community that makes our school a standout choice in Marylebone.
Executive Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Bryanston Square CofE Primary School - Collective Worship
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
Each and every day our school community comes together for collective worship, this act of daily worship is at the heart of our school. Worship and prayer provides our school community the opportunity to come together as one body. As a Church of England school, our daily act of collective worship is centred on Christianity and our core Christian values.
During our daily acts of collective worship we ensure that we are providing worship which is inspirational, inclusive and invitational. We use the aims below to ensure that children and adults in our school community are given the opportunity to develop spirituality through experiences of prayer, stillness, worship and reflection:
Every day, a different member of staff or clergy leads our collective worship:
Monday worship: the Headteacher or a member of the leadership team will lead worship in line with the school vision and values.
Tuesday worship: is led by our RE & Collective Worship Lead with a focus on justice.
Wednesday worship is led by the clergy or member of St Mary's Church Youth Team.
Thursday worship is led by our Music lead, the whole school comes together and worships through song.
Friday worship is led by a member of the leadership team. During this worship we celebrate our success linked to our school values.
We celebrate the major Christian festivals throughout the year. Parents and carers are invited to join us, either at school, or at our Parish Church; St Mary's Bryanston Square. These include the Christmas, Epiphany, Ash Wednesday, Holy Week, Easter and Harvest services.
At the end of every half term we will hold our worship in our Parish Church, St Mary's Bryanston Square. Parents and carers are warmly welcomed to join us whenever we attend the church.
Withdrawal from Collective Worship
As a Church of England school, we are committed to respecting individual beliefs. We celebrate and value the cultural diversity of all the members of our school and we have a cohesive community. Although collective worship will always reflect the Christian ethos of our school, we respect and acknowledge the variety of religious observances which are represented in our school and within the wider community. We acknowledge too that there are those of no faith who chose to be part of our school community.
Upon entrance to the school, parents/ carers are made aware of the Christian basis of our teaching. It is therefore unlikely that parents/carers would wish to exercise their legal right of withdrawal. However, should such a case arise, the parents/carers concerned should consult the Head teacher.
For further information please refer to our Collective Worship Policy.

pageCache.text:
St Mary’s Bryanston Square Church
We are a Church of England primary school, with close links to our parish Church.
We have services in the Church six times a year, led by Revd Matt Coombs, who is one of our school Governors. The Church’s children’s worker, Kirstine and Annabelle, lead Collective Worship every week in school for Early Years, KS1 and KS2, as well as running an extra-curricular club for the children called ‘Star Club’.
The church leads activities all year round, which children from St Mary’s can access, eg a week long holiday club in August and weekly Sunday School ‘SMKC’ which meets in the school hall.
Through the year, we hold special services in church specially for school families, in which our children take part, eg singing in the choir on Mothering Sunday.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Bryanston Square CofE Primary School - Vision & Values
pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
Our school vision and values are at the core of everything we do. They underpin our teaching and learning, and provide an environment which prepares our pupils as confident, happy citizens.
Vision and Values
We are a Church of England primary school with a strong distinctive Christian ethos. Our vision for the school is:
'Excellence with Compassion'
Our vision is based upon Jesus’ commandment in Mark 12:31:
‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength. And love your neighbour as yourself.’ (Mark 12:30-31)
As a Church school, we believe every child is made in the image of God, and therefore we want the very best for them. That means achieving the highest possible academic standards, but also means that we value the whole child – mind, body and spirit – and seek to create a culture of love, respect, wellbeing and safety for everyone in our community.
As a result, we aim to value ourselves as special and unique, value each other and treat each other with kindness, respect and grace, and value families and communities as the places where love can flourish.
At St Mary’s we welcome everyone to be part of our school community; as well as a number of Christian families, many of our children are Muslim or from other faith backgrounds. This is a real strength of our school, and part of what makes our school community such a wonderful place.
We have 6 core values, rooted in our Christian faith, which have been chosen by the pupils, parents, staff and Governors of our school:
RESPECT | HONESTY | FORGIVENESS
FEELING SAFE | LOVE | CURIOSITY
Each value is connected to a verse from the Bible, showing the theological basis underpinning them:

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Bryanston Square CofE Primary School - About Us
pageCache.text:
About Us
History of St Mary’s School
The school was originally founded in 1824 in York Street, next to the parish church, and served a wide area until other local schools were built. An Infants’ schoolroom was added in 1888 but destroyed in an air raid in 1944. In 1969 it moved to a new building in Enford Street, and in 2000 a Nursery Class was added.
St Mary's is a one form entry school in Marylebone, central London. We are a happy school, built on core values which underpin all that we do. The staff team and school community work incredibly well together to ensure that everyone at St Mary's Bryanston Square Primary thrives!
We are a Good school (May 2023), with 4 out of 5 areas graded OUTSTANDING where:
'Pupils love attending this small ‘village’ school. They enjoy learning the broad curriculum, and they comment that their learning is always fun. They work hard and are thoughtful towards others. Pupils appreciate the support that their teachers give them. They speak about how they are always helped to do their best, commenting that they feel very safe.
The school is a cheerful and harmonious place. Pupils behave with high levels of kindness and respect for others. Bullying is very rare. If it does occur, it is dealt with swiftly and effectively. Pupils support and listen to one another.
Leaders have high expectations of all pupils, including those with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND). Pupils read enthusiastically. They learn a broad range of subjects and are taught how to make connections between subject content in different areas of the curriculum. Their learning is enriched by frequent trips and events, and pupils value this.'

Read our full Ofsted Report here: https://reports.ofsted.gov.uk/provider/21/101136 (May 2023)
Our school provides a broad and balanced education for all our children; one which excites the children and helps them to develop a thirst for knowledge. We want every child to achieve as highly as they can, in all areas of learning and life enabling them to become proud citizens of our community.
Children are proud of their school and seek to make it a harmonious place for every member of the school community. We are very well supported by our parents in striving to provide our children with a safe, nurturing environment in which to learn.
The school has an active ‘Friends’ association that includes parents and staff. The Friends have worked hard in recent years to both fundraise for projects, including redeveloping our school library, and to encourage all parents to become involved in the school. Employees from some local businesses also volunteer on a regular basis; supporting children with their reading and learning about Maths and Science.
We have a strong relationship with our Church, St Mary’s Bryanston Square, with our church curate and youth worker leading weekly acts of worship and running prayer clubs in school for the children.
We are very proud of our whole school community, and we always enjoy welcoming visitors to St Mary’s.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Bryanston Square CofE Primary School - CLCSP Partnership
pageCache.text:
CLCSP Partnership
Welcome to the Central London Church School Partnership, consisting of three 1-form-entry Church of England schools within the local authorities of Westminster and Camden.
Our schools are uniquely situated in the heart of the capital, ready to serve our communities. As schools within the London Diocesan Boards for Schools (LDBS), we take our mission to educate from one of the founding principles: ‘serving the children of the parish’. Deeply rooted in the Church of England's historic commitment to education, we provide an excellent education inspired by Christian values, welcoming and valuing every child regardless of faith or background.
Although we are a newly formed partnership, we are three schools who each bring a wealth of experience to the group. Our staff teams have a high level of knowledge of their school and its community. The partnership started in April 2025 with St Mary’s Bryanston Square & Christ Church CE (Regent's Park) joining together. In June 2026, St Mary Mags & St Stephen’s joined the partnership, forming the Central London Church School Partnership.
We aim to enable our schools, as small one-form-entry sites, to thrive and serve their communities. We do this by making child-led decisions, setting high expectations and sharing our expertise across the group of schools. As Church of England primary schools, our schools’ vision and values drive our decisions, and we aim to reflect the communities in which we work, responding through our curriculum and decisions.
Working in our schools, we hope and expect that all staff share the same goal:
‘growing in love, learning with purpose and flourishing with strength’
Our goal is to ensure that each child is provided with the experiences, learning, and opportunities that allow them to open any door they wish in the future.
The work of Senior Leadership is to create the conditions and environment where teachers can teach, children can learn, and everyone feels happy and safe.
Our three schools, St Mary’s Bryanston Square CE Primary, Christ Church CE (Regents Park) Primary & St Mary Magdalene & St Stephen’s Primary Schools, are working together to provide high-quality education to children in our communities of Westminster and Camden. We do this in line with the vision and values of each school, whilst underpinned by the founding principles of church schools;
What this means for us as CLCSP is;
Our partnership believes that our schools should have space to share their unique identities and responsiveness to their individual communities; therefore, each school retains its own vision and values. We have shared the overview for each school below:
St Mary's Bryanston Square CE Primary School
'Excellence with Compassion'
Our vision is based upon Jesus’ commandment in Mark 12:31:
‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength. And love your neighbour as yourself.’ (Mark 12:30-31)
Christ Church CE Primary School (Regent's Park)
At Christ Church, we all care, learn and work together for God and others.
‘For we are all God’s handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance for us to do’. Ephesians 2:10
St Mary Mag's & St Stephen's CE Primary School (MMSTS)
"I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me." Philippians 4:13
‘Children are great imitators, so give them something great to imitate’
As a staff team we model the expectations for our pupils through personal and professional conduct. This is in both words and actions.
CLCSP Partnership

PE and Sport Premium
What is the PE and sport premium grant?
The government provides funding worth £320 million per year to support its aim of giving children the opportunity to live healthy and active lives. This money goes directly to primary schools to spend on improving the quality of sport and PE for all their children. This means that St Mary's is allocated around an average of £17,000 each year.
The PE and sport premium funding is used to:
support all children and young people to live healthy, active lives
make participation in PE and school sport easier
make sure all children can achieve and thrive through increased physical activity and sport, no matter their background or ability
improve children’s health, wellbeing, personal development and academic attainment
embed the foundations of positive and enjoyable participation in regular physical activity.

As a parent governor, I support the school’s vision and values by bringing both a parent’s perspective and my experience as a headteacher of a Nursery School. This helps me to understand the needs of pupils, staff, and families. I aim to work with other governors and school leaders to help maintain high standards, support positive behaviour, and promote an inclusive environment where all children can succeed. I also aim to help the school by offering practical ideas, sharing my experience of school improvement, and strengthening communication between the school and parents, so that the school’s values are reflected in everything it does.

Remote Learning Offer
Remote Education Provision: Information for Families
This information is intended to provide clarity and transparency to pupils and parents or carers about what to expect from remote education where cohorts need to remain at home.
‘Remote Education’ is what happens when the school or part of the school has to close.
Our Remote Education offer includes online learning and printed resources. Google Classroom will be the primary tool used to provide online guidance from teachers to support learning outside of school.
We are aware that no two families are the same so adaptations can be made for those who require it.
Please contact us on 020 3146 0968 or via office@stmbs.org.uk if you need any support.
